full_judgment:
2. The preemption petitioner claimed preemption in respect of the suit land by filing an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act alleging, inter alia, that he was a co-sharer tenant of the disputed Khatian by inheritance. But the premptee opposite party No.3 sold the suit land to the preemptee opposite parties Nos.1 and 2, who were strangers, without issuing of any notice of sale. 

 4. The trial Court as well as the appellate Court below dismissed the preemption on the finding that the preemptor petitioner ceased to have any right of pre-emption as he had no subsisting interest in the disputed Khatian. During the pendency of the appeal the pre-emptor petitioner filed an application for amendment of the pre-emption application in order to incorporate certain new facts showing that he was a co-sharer tenant in the disputed Khatian not only by way of inheritance but also by way of purchase.
